holdings.name: ICICI Bank Ltd

what_changed.text: ICICI Bank received a West Bengal GST show-cause notice demanding ₹16.76 crore on minimum-balance services.
The bank scheduled a board meeting on October 17, 2026, to review and approve Q2 FY27 standalone and consolidated results.

holdings.why_it_matters: ICICI Bank is the largest fund holding at 5.67%. Its 1-month drop of -7.22% and 3-month drop of -4.37% drag fund returns directly across the heavily weighted Financials allocation (31.1%).

watch.text: Board meeting outcome and Q2 FY27 financial results on October 17, 2026.

holdings.name: Bharat Electronics Ltd

what_changed.text: Bharat Electronics secured additional orders worth ₹648 crore since August 26, 2026.
The company appointed M/s Rao & Emmar as statutory auditors for FY 2026-27.

holdings.why_it_matters: At 5.40% portfolio weight, BEL is the second-largest holding, meaning its -3.35% 3-month performance exerts a noticeable drag on the fund's 14.6% Industrials bucket.

watch.text: Order execution updates and progress on new defence manufacturing contracts.

holdings.name: HDFC Bank Ltd

what_changed.text: HDFC Bank's board approved a list of CEO candidates, reappointed V. Srinivasa Rangan, appointed Jimmy Tata, and added a whole-time director post.
The board is set to meet on October 17, 2026, to consider Q2 and H1 FY27 results, with trading window closed from September 24 to October 19.

holdings.why_it_matters: Holding a 4.97% fund weight, HDFC Bank's 3-month return of -7.62% shaved an estimated -0.379% off fund performance, ranking it among the top five detractors.

watch.text: RBI decision on the new CEO appointment and Q2 FY27 results on October 17, 2026.

holdings.name: State Bank of India

what_changed.text: SBI shifted the bond interest payment date for ISIN INE062A08397 to September 27, 2026.
SBI conducted investor interactions via Jefferies in Gurugram and virtually through Citi.

holdings.why_it_matters: Holding a 4.47% fund weight, SBI's 1-month decline of -6.56% and 3-month loss of -5.97% compound the recent weakness across the fund's top banking names.

watch.text: Institutional investor presentation updates and operational guidance from recent meets.

holdings.name: Zomato Ltd

what_changed.text: Eternal received an ESG score of 76.00 with a Leader band rating for FY2026, alongside a separate CRISIL ESG rating of 72.
Zomato introduced a new 'pay-on-delivery' surcharge across its delivery operations.

holdings.why_it_matters: Representing 4.07% of the fund, Zomato gained 31.30% over 3 months, acting as the fund's single largest performance contributor (+1.274%).

watch.text: Competitive intensity in quick commerce against peers in the medium term.

holdings.name: Jindal Steel & Power Ltd

what_changed.text: SEBI fined two designated persons of Jindal Steel for trading-window violations.
The company scheduled and held analyst and institutional investor meetings throughout August and September 2026.

holdings.why_it_matters: With a 4.02% fund weight, JSPL's 9.94% 3-month return added +0.400% to fund performance, buffering broader cyclical weakness.

watch.text: Updates from upcoming analyst interactions and institutional investor schedules.

holdings.name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd

what_changed.text: L&T Semiconductor introduced 40 products at SEMICON 2026, including its initial silicon carbide chips.
Larsen & Toubro secured an ammonia plant revamp order worth ₹797 crore from Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilisers, plus an offshore contract from ONGC.

holdings.why_it_matters: Holding a 3.73% fund weight, L&T shed -8.07% over 3 months, creating an estimated -0.301% performance headwind.

watch.text: Commercial execution of semiconductor offerings and order inflow momentum.

holdings.name: Axis Bank Ltd

what_changed.text: Axis Bank appointed Arvind Subramanian as an additional independent director for four years starting September 23, 2026.
The bank engaged institutional investors at the CLSA 33rd Investors Forum in Hong Kong.

holdings.why_it_matters: Axis Bank makes up 3.69% of the fund. Its -11.24% 3-month return subtracted -0.415% from fund gains, ranking as the second-largest holding detractor.

watch.text: Potential fee income pressure stemming from IRDAI insurance distribution reforms.

holdings.name: Solar Industries India Ltd

what_changed.text: Solar Industries proposed a $1.35 billion acquisition of Omnia Holdings, leading ICRA to assign [ICRA]A1+ to its commercial paper and CRISIL to place its loans on rating watch developing.
The company repaid a ₹75 crore commercial paper on its maturity date of September 17, 2026.

holdings.why_it_matters: Allocated at 3.57%, Solar Industries rallied 13.29% over 3 months, generating +0.474% in fund contribution, the second-highest across holdings.

watch.text: Regulatory and operational progress regarding the proposed Omnia Holdings acquisition.

holdings.name: SRF Ltd

what_changed.text: KAMA Realty acquired shares of SRF from KAMA Holdings via off-market inter-se transfers, taking its stake to 1.01% with no change in control.
Chief Human Resources Officer Geeta Shamrao Jadhav resigned effective September 23, 2026.

holdings.why_it_matters: Holding 2.82% of the fund, SRF declined -7.06% over 3 months and -1.66% over 1 month, softening the performance of the fund's 16.2% Materials allocation.

watch.text: Leadership transitions following the resignation of the CHRO.

portfolio.statement: Kotak Flexi Cap Fund maintains an equity exposure of 98.6% with top 10 holdings accounting for 42.4% of total AUM.
interp: The portfolio exhibits heavy sector concentration in Financials (31.1%), Materials (16.2%), and Industrials (14.6%).
Recent 3-month performance shows sharp divergence between strong gains in Technology and Materials against widespread drawdowns in large banking holdings.
portfolio.line: Returns over 3 months (-2.25%) reflect dragging Financials positions offset by sharp rallies in Zomato and Solar Industries.

drivers.text: Zomato returned 31.3% over 3 months, adding an estimated +1.274% to fund performance.
Solar Industries gained 13.29% over 3 months, contributing +0.474% to returns.
Axis Bank dropped -11.24% and HDFC Bank fell -7.62% over 3 months, subtracting -0.415% and -0.379% respectively.

themes.title: Private Banking Exposure
themes.text: Concentrated exposure across top private and public lenders faced broad pressure over the recent quarter.

themes.title: Capital Goods and Industrial Expansion
themes.text: Holdings tied to domestic defence, offshore engineering, and semiconductor expansion are securing steady order books.

macro.why: IRDAI scrutiny over insurance commission payouts has pressured fee income expectations across private banking holdings.
Cross-border acquisitions are prompting credit rating watch adjustments while firms pursue overseas expansion.

priced_in.text: Solar Industries' market valuation of 86.12 P/E reflects elevated growth expectations following its proposed Omnia acquisition.

could_change.text: Regulatory approval and onboarding of new top leadership at HDFC Bank could reshape strategic direction.

could_change.title: Closing of Cross-Border Acquisitions
could_change.text: Finalisation or structural adjustments to Solar Industries' $1.35 billion acquisition of Omnia could shift debt profiles and credit ratings.

portfolio.risk_note: Financials represent 31.1% of the fund; synchronized corrections in major bank holdings like ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and Axis Bank create substantial downside risk to overall fund NAV.
